name: Simple Combat Foundation
designRule: Basic combat uses one attack roll, fixed damage, one Protection value, and Vitality loss. Extra attack successes never increase damage.

coreProcedure.start: Combat begins when opposed actions become time-sensitive enough that acting first changes the result. Establish positions, cover, visible threats, current tracks, and immediate objectives before Initiative.
coreProcedure.initiative: Initiative equals Finesse + Composure. Act from highest Initiative to lowest. Break ties with higher Awareness, then higher Finesse, then one unmodified d10 roll.
coreProcedure.round: A round is approximately six seconds. Each participant receives one turn per round.
coreProcedure.turn: On a turn, take one Standard Action, move up to 8 meters, and perform one Minor Interaction in any order. A Standard Action may become another Move or Minor Interaction. Unused actions are lost.
coreProcedure.reaction: A character has one Reaction per round. It refreshes at the start of that character's turn and may be used only when a rule, capability, item, or Cohesion option allows it.
coreProcedure.minorInteraction: Draw or stow one accessible item, open or close one unsecured adjacent closure, change posture, shift form when permitted, speak briefly, or press one adjacent control.

basicLoop: Build the attack pool from the printed Attribute and Skill.
Add one die for every Exposure point currently carried by the target.
Subtract dice for range, cover, conditions, and equipment.
Roll against Defense Difficulty, which equals ceiling(Guard / 2), minimum 1.
On a hit, use the attack's fixed Damage rating. Extra successes add nothing.
Subtract one applicable Protection value. Disruption normally ignores Protection.
Remove one Vitality for each point remaining.
pools: Unarmed or forceful melee: Force + Close Combat.
Heavy weapon: Force + Heavy Weapons unless the item states otherwise.
Damaging capability: use the pool printed by the capability.
attackProcedure.hit: Successes equal to or above Defense Difficulty hit. Extra successes do not change damage.
attackProcedure.fixedDamage: Every weapon and damaging ability has one fixed Damage rating.
attackProcedure.protection: Impact and Trauma subtract one applicable Protection value from fixed Damage, minimum 0. Disruption ignores ordinary Protection unless a rule explicitly protects against it.
attackProcedure.vitalityLoss: Every point remaining after Protection removes 1 current Vitality.
cover: Total Cover: no direct attack unless an effect crosses or destroys it.
range: Beyond Long: unavailable unless explicitly allowed.

damageAndVitality.impact: Impact represents bruising, blunt force, shock, fatigue, and nonpenetrating injury.
damageAndVitality.trauma: Trauma represents penetration, severe laceration, burning, crushing, organ injury, and other dangerous bodily harm.
damageAndVitality.disruption: Disruption represents memory damage, identity fracture, noospheric injury, hostile cognition, and damage to functional continuity.
damageAndVitality.sharedTrack: All damage types remove points from the same current Vitality track. Record type separately because healing and defenses may treat them differently.
damageAndVitality.noWoundedBand: At 1 or more Vitality, act normally unless a specific condition says otherwise. There is no universal Wounded state or penalty.
damageAndVitality.healing: Removing one recorded damage point restores one current Vitality. Current Vitality cannot exceed Maximum.

exposure.meaning: Exposure is how open, predictable, or easy to target the character has become.
gain: After a Push resolves, gain 1 Exposure.
A hazard, capability, or Complication adds Exposure only when it explicitly says so.
exposure.combatEffect: Every Exposure point on a target adds one die to attacks against that target. Exposure affects accuracy only, never damage or Protection.
exposure.push: Reroll failed dice up to Resolve once. Keep the new results and gain 1 Exposure after resolution.
exposure.limit: When Exposure reaches its Limit, finish the action and resolve Overexposure.
exposure.overexposure: Suffer 1 Impact ignoring Protection, lose the current Reaction, and reset Exposure to 0. Exposure has no Warning or Critical band.
recovery: Ten uninterrupted minutes free from combat, pursuit, and active hazards sets Exposure to 0.
A Full Rest sets Exposure to 0.

cohesion.meaning: Cohesion is deliberately spent to stay effective under immediate danger. It is not another automatic damage track.
cohesion.spendingLimit: Use only one Cohesion option on the same trigger or test unless a capability explicitly says otherwise.

options.name: Commit
options.effect: Add two dice to that test.

options.name: Brace
options.effect: Reduce remaining Impact or Disruption by 1. Brace cannot reduce Trauma.

options.name: Anchor
options.timing: Reaction when an ally makes a Death Test or a test against involuntary control
options.effect: The ally rerolls up to two failed dice and keeps the new results.

options.name: Refuse Collapse
options.timing: Once per scene when damage would reduce positive Vitality to 0
options.effect: Remain at 1 Vitality and become Staggered until the end of the next turn. It cannot stop explicit instant death or be used while Downed.

recovery: Once per scene after immediate danger ends, ten uninterrupted minutes regrouping with a willing ally restores 1 Cohesion.
A completed Full Rest restores Cohesion to Maximum.

pressureInCombat.rule: Pay Resource, mark printed Pressure, resolve the ability, then resolve a Crisis if Pressure reached its Limit.
pressureInCombat.thresholdTiming: Warning or Critical effects begin after the action that crossed the threshold resolves. A Critical rule already active before the expenditure applies normally.
pressureInCombat.persistence: Pressure remains after combat until the Archetype's printed recovery methods reduce it.
pressureInCombat.distinction: Exposure makes enemies more accurate. Pressure creates the Archetype's specific loss of control, mutation, hunger, instability, or overload.

shapechangerSoak.name: Living Soak
shapechangerSoak.singleDefenseRule: Living Soak modifies the Shapechanger's one Protection value. It creates no second roll or second damage step.
shapechangerSoak.socialForm: Add Archetype Rating to Protection against Impact only.
shapechangerSoak.huntingAndWarForms: Add Archetype Rating to Protection against Impact and Trauma.
shapechangerSoak.completeNegation: If fixed Damage does not exceed the resulting Protection, the hit deals 0 damage.
shapechangerSoak.excludedEffects: Disruption, Pressure, Exposure, and Death Marks bypass Living Soak.

conditions.prone: Standing costs the Move. Adjacent melee attacks gain one die; ranged attacks from more than 3 meters lose one die.
conditions.restrained: Movement is 0. Attacks against the target gain one die. Most physical tests lose two dice except Break Free.
conditions.staggered: The character has no Reaction and loses one die from tests until the condition ends.
conditions.downed: Current Vitality is 0. The character is Prone, cannot act or move, and is Unstable unless stabilized.
conditions.stable: A Stable character remains Downed at 0 Vitality but makes no Death Tests. New damage makes the character Unstable again.

downedDyingAndDeath.reachingZero: When damage reduces Vitality to 0, become Downed and Unstable. Every damage point remaining after Vitality reaches 0 adds 1 Death Mark. At 3 Death Marks, the character dies immediately.
downedDyingAndDeath.gracePeriod: A character reduced to 0 makes no Death Test during that round. If still Unstable, the first Death Test occurs at the end of the following round.
downedDyingAndDeath.deathTest: Roll Resilience + Composure at difficulty 2. Success adds no Death Mark. Failure adds 1. A failed roll containing a 1 adds 2 instead. The test may be Pushed or receive Anchor.
downedDyingAndDeath.furtherDamage: A new damaging hit against a Downed character adds 1 Death Mark, or 2 when the hit deals 3 or more damage.
downedDyingAndDeath.stabilize: Standard Action, adjacent target. Test Reason + Medicine at difficulty 2 with a field medical kit or 3 without one. Success makes the target Stable and removes 1 Death Mark.
downedDyingAndDeath.emergencyTreatment: Standard Action, adjacent Stable target at 0 Vitality, one field medical kit charge. Test Reason + Medicine at difficulty 3. Success removes one Impact or Trauma, restores 1 Vitality, removes 1 Death Mark, ends Downed, and applies Staggered through the target's next turn.
downedDyingAndDeath.death: At 3 Death Marks the character is dead. Ordinary healing, Cohesion, Stabilize, Emergency Treatment, and retroactive declarations cannot reverse death.
downedDyingAndDeath.equalApplication: Player characters, allies, neutral characters, and enemies use the same Downed and death rules unless a recorded capability says otherwise.
